answer: Bonded sponsorship makes Sybil attacks expensive: a newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes a deposit on its conduct, forfeited if it spams or cheats, and each sponsor may back only a few newcomers. Faking thousands of identities then costs real collateral instead of free clicks. Think of the bond as a walnut shell, hard to crack open cheaply; a cluster of self-vouching fakes stands out like an ivory tower against the wider trust graph; and like a glacier, the stake thaws slowly, so attackers cannot strike and vanish before the penalty lands.
